author: DTrim99
body:
Thanks, this return matches the income (federal AGI $125,421). Two things account for the whole gap between TaxAct's Georgia AGI ($107,876) and ours ($119,822.77).

**1. The ages differ from the input row.** Form 500 lines 6a/6b give dates of birth 01/01/1954 and 02/02/1954, so TaxAct treats both spouses as 70. The input row has `page=60`, `sage=66`. A 60-year-old can't take the exclusion, so we give the primary $0, where TaxAct's worksheet gives $5,599 ($5,000 of wages plus $599 of interest).

**2. TaxAct counts the spouse's $6,347 of UI as retirement income.** It enters it on Line 10, "Other Income", of the spouse's Retirement Income Exclusion worksheet, which raises the spouse's exclusion from $5,599 to $11,946. That's the 6347 you saw. PolicyEngine doesn't count UI toward the exclusion, and neither does TAXSIM (08-13 build).

| | Ages | UI counted? | GA AGI |
|---|---|---|---|
| PolicyEngine = TAXSIM 08-13, your input | 60 / 66 | no | 119,822.77 |
| PolicyEngine = TAXSIM 08-13, TaxAct's ages | 70 / 70 | no | 114,223.72 |
| TaxAct | 70 / 70 | yes | 107,876 |

Taking the $6,347 of UI out of the 70/70 case gives $107,877.05, TaxAct's figure to the dollar. (The current 09-01 TAXSIM build gives $124,822.77 on your input because it drops the 2024 Georgia exclusion; see #1208.)

Is UI retirement income in Georgia? Neither the regulation nor the booklet names it. Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 560-7-4-.02(4)(b)(1) defines the unearned portion as:
> "interest income, dividend income, net income or loss from rental property … capital gains or losses, income from royalties, income from pensions and annuities, and other similar income."

The earned portion covers business income and "wages, salaries, tips, and other employer compensation." The [2024 IT-511 (p. 24)](https://dor.georgia.gov/document/document/2024-it-511-individual-income-tax-booklet/download#page=24) says only:
> "Social Security and Railroad Retirement paid by the Railroad Retirement Board, exempt interest, or other income that is not taxable to Georgia should not be included in the retirement income exclusion calculation."

UI is taxable in Georgia. But it isn't earned income, and it isn't much like interest or a pension, so we read "other similar income" as not covering it; TaxAct reads it the other way. Do you know of Georgia guidance on this? If Georgia allows it, our change would be to add UI to the exclusion's income list (`gov.states.ga.tax.income.agi.exclusions.retirement.sources`).
